title: Darkness and light
hookLine: praise to Allah who created the heavens and earth and made darkness and light (6:1)
last: ISA'S ANSWER — ONLY WHAT I WAS TOLD.

cards: Surah six is al-An'am, the Cattle, named for a passage near its middle about the herds and the customs people built around them.
It's a Meccan surah, from the years before the move to Medina, and tradition says it came down all at once rather than in pieces.
It also opens with words you learned on day eleven of this path, the same words that open al-Fatiha: al-hamdu lillah. Then, in the very first verse, it does something quietly strange with grammar.

teach.b: Here's the verse, in Pickthall's words: “Praise be to Allah, Who hath created the heavens and the earth, and hath appointed darkness and light.” Listen to the two verbs. The heavens and the earth are created, khalaqa.
Darkness and light are appointed, made, set in place, ja'ala. Some commentators read ja'ala here as giving something its role, its job. Now the two nouns.
In Arabic, darkness is plural, az-zulumat, darknesses.
Light is singular, an-nur. The Qur'an keeps that shape when it uses the pair: in 2:257, Allah brings believers out of the darknesses into the light.

Some commentators read it as a picture: many ways to be lost, and one way home. Later in this same surah, a verse says this is My straight path, so follow it, and don't follow the other paths that scatter you.
Darknesses, many. Light, one. But the verse doesn't treat darkness as an enemy that slipped in.
It opens with praise for the One who made both.

teach.h: NIGHT IS PART OF THE DESIGN.
teach.b: Night is part of the design: the time for rest, the backdrop for stars, the dark before the dawn prayer.
And the end of the verse turns, almost sadly: yet those who disbelieve set up equals to their Lord.
The whole surah will keep returning to this: look at the sky, the seeds, the night and the day, and ask who set them in place.
Light and darkness come first, perhaps because everyone sees them, every day, at dusk and at dawn.

how: Muslims read the opening of al-An'am as a call to see Allah in the order of creation; its first verse opens with al-hamdu lillah, as al-Fatiha does, and some recite the surah in full as a devotion.

games.q: you're reading the first verse of al-An'am. which verb does it use for darkness and light?
games.why: ja'ala: appointed, given a role. the heavens and the earth get khalaqa, created.

practice: If you can, sit by a window at dusk, when the day is still in the sky and the dark is already coming; if not, turn off one light and leave another on.
Notice the light on one side of your face and the shadow on the other, neither a mistake, each doing its job.

wordCard.voice: Az-zulumat. Darkness, in the plural: the Qur'an's word for how many ways there are to be lost, before the one path of light.

orig.note: Arabic: the darknesses (plural) and the light (singular), from 6:1.

carryVoice: Your line: he made both. Darknesses, many; light, one; both set in place. See you tomorrow.
